narrative_purpose: Show an ore body as the record of long-lived fluid flow that it is, so the mining question lands as a geological one about circulating water and heat.
subject: A close underground view of a wall of fractured dark rock. Threading through it is a dense branching network of pale mineral veins, ranging from hairline threads to bands a hand's width across, following the fracture pattern and visibly thickening and pooling where two or more veins intersect. Within the widest vein sections, small angular metallic crystals catch the light with a cold sheen. The host rock around each vein is discoloured in a narrow bleached halo, paler than the rock further away. At the very bottom of the frame the rock takes on a faint dull ember warmth, as though heat is rising from below out of view.
scene: A cut face of mineralized rock deep underground on Pandora, lit only by the faint glow of the mineral itself and heat from below.
camera: Close, nearly flat-on to the rock face, filling the frame so the vein network is the entire subject.
light: Faint cool cyan self-glow from the metallic crystals in the veins; dull ember-amber gradient rising from the very bottom edge; the host rock otherwise in deep indigo darkness.
palette: Void-indigo and obsidian host rock, pale grey-white vein mineral, cold cyan glints on the metallic crystals, restrained dull ember-amber confined to the lowest strip of the frame.
style: Painterly petrological specimen plate, heavy rock and crystal texture, close observed detail, naturalist rather than dramatic.
detail_level: High detail throughout — individual vein branches, crystal faces, and the bleached halos in the host rock all crisp.
composition: Vein network branching diagonally across the frame from lower left to upper right, thickening toward the centre where several intersect; areas of plain dark host rock left uncluttered on the right and upper left.
consistency_notes: No mining machinery or human presence — this is the rock itself. Cool palette dominant; the ember warmth is a single narrow gradient at the bottom edge only, standing for heat from depth.
